Subject: Flexible onramp & invoice milestones for Dedicated commit

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers looked great for our streaming use case. Before we get legal involved I wanted to confirm a couple of commercial details around the Dedicated reserved commit options you shared (12 / 24 / 36 month):

- UnityTech needs a soft start: we plan to begin customer-facing traffic in Q1 2027 but would like a two-phase activation (pilot -> full) so we only pay full committed capacity after the pilot window. Can you support staged activation where the invoice schedule is milestone-driven rather than a single start date?
- We prefer to split payments across three milestone invoices tied to pilot completion, production go-live, and 30 days post-go-live. Are there standard invoice templates you use for this split?
- For sizing: target steady-state is ~120T tokens per second across our fleet. We initially asked for a 16-GPU A100 pool but would consider a combination (e.g., mix of A100 80GB for encoders + H100 for heavy decoding). Any guidance on performance per-GPU for the throughput target?

If you can send a milestone-friendly commercial that shows pricing for 12/24/36mo with the split-invoice option and the related SLA/throughput guarantees, I’ll route to contracts and procurement. We’re aiming to finalize commercial terms by 2026-09-20.

Best,
Maria Lopez
Head of AI Ops, UnityTech

Hi Maria — appreciate the clear ask. High-level answers below and attaching a draft that maps the three milestone invoices to activation triggers (see attached).

- Staged activation: yes, we can structure the reserved commit so billing ramps with activation milestones. Typical approach we use: 10% deposit to reserve capacity at contract signature, 40% invoice at pilot-to-production handoff (when you flip traffic >=50% to Redwood Dedicated), and remaining 50% on production steady-state (30 days after full traffic cutover). We include a formal "activation certificate" signed by both parties to mark milestone completion.
- Invoice templates: attached spreadsheet (milestone-invoice-schedule.xlsx) shows suggested line-items (monthly run-rate vs prepaid commit credit). We can convert to your PO format once legal signs.
- Sizing & throughput guidance: based on our benchmarks, a single A100 80GB (quantized) can sustain ~7-9T tokens/sec for mixed short/long sequences with batching; an H100 can be ~10-12T tokens/sec depending on model family and quantization. For ~120T target, a reasonable starting pool is 12x H100-equivalent or 16-18x A100-equivalent. If you want headroom for peak spikes, we recommend a +20% buffer and burst capacity policy.

I’ve looped Ben (pricing) and Lauren (legal ops) to put numbers on the three term options and confirm SLA language. Ben / Lauren — can you propose: (a) list pricing for 12/24/36 mo (per GPU-month committed rate and percentage discount vs on-demand), (b) suggested credit/refund schedule if activation is delayed beyond agreed windows, and (c) throughput guarantee verbiage tied to token/sec and percent uptime? Maria asked for terms by 9/20 — can we aim to have a proposed commercial by 9/15 so she has time to share with procurement?

Thanks,
Aditya

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Pricing draft for UnityTech (milestone billing + activation windows)

Quick draft for the business — numbers are illustrative but conservative. Putting it here so Aditya can send a clean version to Maria.

Assumptions: steady-state target 120T tokens/sec, activation buffer +20%, equivalent pool sizing = 15 H100-equivalent GPUs.

Pricing (committed per-GPU-month equivalent, billed as prepaid credits against monthly consumption):
- 12 months: $27,000 / GPU-month (baseline) — approx 18% discount vs on-demand
- 24 months: $23,000 / GPU-month — approx 30% discount vs on-demand
- 36 months: $20,500 / GPU-month — approx 40% discount vs on-demand

Milestone invoice schedule (recommended):
- Invoice 1 (10% deposit at signature): covers reservation and initial onboarding.
- Invoice 2 (40% at pilot-to-prod handoff): due when activation certificate signed and traffic >=50% routed.
- Invoice 3 (50% at steady-state): due 30 days after full cutover.

Activation windows / delay protection:
- Standard start window: 90 days from signature to pilot activation. If activation delayed beyond this, customer has two options: (a) extend start window with no penalty for up to 60 days, or (b) request a pro-rata hold with a monthly reservation fee equal to 10% of committed monthly spend.
- If activation is delayed >150 days, we offer a one-time credit equal to 5% of committed value or push the term start-date (mutually agreed).

Throughput SLA (proposal):
- We guarantee 99.5% availability for the committed pool during business hours (8am–8pm customer's local) and 99.0% 24x7. Throughput guarantee: committed pool will deliver within ±10% of the measured token/sec benchmark for each model family under agreed test harness; benchmark and model version to be defined in the SOW. Remedies: service credits tiered by duration of underperformance (e.g., 5% credit for 6–24 hours, 10% for 24–72 hours).

Notes on mixing GPU types: we can present a blended price if UnityTech wants a hybrid pool (e.g., 10x H100 + 6x A100). Any mixed pool requires an explicit routing policy and a fallback mapping in case of capacity constraints.

Next steps: Aditya — if you want, I can prepare a short commercial spreadsheet with the three term rows and milestone invoices broken out. Lauren, can you check the activation window language and suggest legal-safe wording for the activation certificate?

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Strategy, Redwood Inference
